Present and interpret results using tables and block graphs.
Identify, name and describe the basic parts of the human body.
Identify the senses (touch, taste, smell, sight and hearing) and the body parts associated with each sense.
Recognise that humans and animals have offspring that grow into adults.
Identify living things and things that have never been alive.
Recognise that animals, including humans, need water, food and air to survive.
Identify animals and plants in their local environment and observe how they change over time.
Identify, name and describe common everyday materials including wood, plastic, metal, glass, rock, paper and fabric.
Understand that objects are made from materials that have specific properties.
Describe properties of materials using words such as hard, soft, rough, smooth, bendy and waterproof.
Sort materials according to their observable properties.
Explore pushes and pulls as forces that can change the motion or shape of objects.
Explore how things move on different surfaces.
Identify sources of sound and understand that sounds travel to our ears.
Identify sources of light, including the Sun, and understand that darkness is the absence of light.
Observe and describe the weather and how it changes across the seasons.
Identify the Sun, Moon, stars and clouds in the sky.
Sort and classify objects, materials and living things using simple criteria.
Use given equipment safely and make simple measurements.
Make predictions and suggest ways to collect evidence.
Record observations in simple tables, tallies and pictograms.
Identify and name the major external parts of flowering plants (roots, stem, leaves, flowers).
Recognise that plants need light, water and suitable temperature to grow and stay healthy.
Describe the life cycle of flowering plants including seed germination, growth and flowering.
Identify simple food chains starting with a plant.
Distinguish between an object and the material from which it is made.
Investigate how materials can be changed by squashing, bending, twisting and stretching.
Explore heating and cooling as processes that can change materials (melting, freezing).
Explore how forces can change the speed and direction of moving objects.
Identify common appliances that run on electricity and understand electrical safety.
Explore how shadows are formed when light is blocked by an opaque object.
Describe rocks and soil found in the local environment.
Describe how day and night are related to the apparent movement of the Sun.
Make objective observations and take measurements using standard units.
Plan fair tests with support, identifying what to change and what to keep the same.
Identify patterns in data and explain whether results support predictions.
Identify the function of different parts of flowering plants (water uptake by roots, support by stem, photosynthesis in leaves).
Identify that humans and some other animals have skeletons and muscles for support, protection and movement.
Recognise that animals need adequate food, water and nutrition to grow and stay healthy.
Explore how different habitats provide for the basic needs of different animals and plants.
Understand that matter exists in three states: solid, liquid and gas.
Investigate the properties of solids, liquids and gases.
Explore how water changes state through melting, freezing, evaporating and condensing.
Investigate gravity as a pulling force towards the centre of the Earth.
Investigate friction as a contact force between moving surfaces.
Explore how vibrations produce sounds and how pitch and volume can change.
Understand that light travels from a source to our eyes or reflects off surfaces.
Understand the structure of the Earth and describe how fossils are formed in sedimentary rocks.
Describe the planetary bodies in the Solar System.
Use apparatus accurately, including measuring cylinders and thermometers.
Formulate scientific questions and hypotheses.
Present scientific conclusions supported by data in tables, line graphs and bar charts.
Identify the human digestive system and the function of organs (mouth, stomach, intestines).
Identify different types of human teeth and their functions in chewing food.
Understand pollination, seed formation and seed dispersal mechanisms in plants.
Construct and interpret food chains and food webs with producers, consumers, predators and prey.
Investigate particle model of matter in solids, liquids and gases.
Explore dissolving and distinguish between solute, solvent and solution.
Investigate how temperature affects the rate of dissolving.
Construct simple series circuits with cells, lamps, switches and buzzers.
Investigate electrical conductors and insulators.
Investigate magnetic forces, magnetic poles and magnetic materials.
Investigate light reflection and transmission through transparent, translucent and opaque materials.
Describe the water cycle including evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection.
Explain how Earth's rotation creates the 24-hour day and night cycle.
Select appropriate measuring instruments and use them with precision.
Identify variables to control in a fair test and design comparative investigations.
Evaluate experimental methods and suggest improvements based on sources of error.
Identify parts of the human circulatory system (heart, blood vessels, blood) and its role in transporting substances.
Identify the human respiratory system (lungs, trachea, diaphragm) and describe gas exchange.
Compare the life cycles of mammals, amphibians, insects and birds.
Investigate how living organisms are adapted to survive in specific ecosystems and environments.
Distinguish between pure substances and mixtures.
Investigate methods of separating mixtures (filtration, evaporation, decanting, sieving, magnetism).
Distinguish between reversible and irreversible chemical changes.
Investigate balanced and unbalanced forces and their effects on movement and shape.
Investigate air resistance, water resistance and friction.
Investigate how sound travels through different mediums (solids, liquids, gases).
Investigate light refraction as it passes between different media.
Describe the orbit of the Earth around the Sun and explain why seasons occur.
Describe the phases of the Moon and lunar orbit around the Earth.
Conduct scientific investigations independently, taking repeat readings and calculating averages.
Identify testable hypotheses and identify independent, dependent and controlled variables.
Analyse complex trends in data, calculate averages, and write structured scientific conclusions.
Describe the human nervous system and sense organs.
Describe the role of micro-organisms (bacteria, fungi, viruses) in health, disease and decomposition.
Describe human growth and development through puberty to adulthood.
Investigate how human activities impact ecosystems, biodiversity and the environment.
Investigate acids and alkalis using indicators (litmus, universal indicator) and the pH scale.
Investigate neutralisation reactions between acids and alkalis.
Investigate chemical reactions (combustion, rusting, oxidation) and signs of chemical change.
Investigate voltage, current and components in series and parallel circuits.
Investigate mass, weight and gravity, understanding weight = mass x gravitational field strength.
Investigate density and floating/sinking.
Investigate how light travels in straight lines and explains periscopes and shadows.
Describe Earth's tectonic plates, earthquakes, volcanoes and the rock cycle.
Describe the Solar System, planets, asteroids, comets and space exploration.
